title: The final challenge
text: The book presents the ultimate test: build a complete privacy-preserving voting system that integrates all concepts learned. This is the boss battle - the integration of everything from witness to Merkle trees. Only by combining all pieces can you succeed.
visualHint: Final exam with all topics from the course

title: What you must integrate
text: The challenge requires combining: witness (private inputs), assert (circuit logic), disclose (selective reveal), nullifier (uniqueness), DUST (cost management), and Merkle trees (membership proofs). Each piece plays a critical role.
visualHint: Puzzle pieces coming together: witness, assert, disclose, nullifier, DUST, Merkle

title: The scenario: private election
text: The book describes a complete election scenario: eligible voters must prove membership without revealing identity, vote encryption must be secret, tallying must be verifiable, and double-voting must be impossible. This is the ultimate test.
visualHint: Election ballot box with privacy shields

title: Why this matters
text: This integration demonstrates real-world privacy-preserving applications. The book shows that only by mastering all these concepts can you build systems that protect user privacy while maintaining integrity. This is the future of voting, airdrops, and more.
visualHint: Trophy or graduation cap marking completion

title: Step 1: Identity and eligibility
text: The book shows how to start: use witness for private identity data, use Merkle tree for eligibility list. The circuit proves the voter is in the list without revealing who they are. This is the foundation.
visualHint: User identity being verified against a Merkle tree

title: Step 2: Vote encryption and commitment
text: Next, use persistentCommit to encrypt the vote. The book explains that the vote is sealed in a commitment, readable only by the election authority. Use disclose to reveal vote count without revealing who voted for whom.
visualHint: Vote being sealed in an encrypted commitment

title: Step 3: Uniqueness with nullifier
text: The nullifier prevents double-voting. The book shows: generate nullifier from secret key + vote event, publish it to ledger, verify it's unique. The circuit uses assert to enforce this. This is the anti-double-vote mechanism.
visualHint: Nullifier being checked in the ledger

title: Step 4: DUST cost management
text: Finally, account for DUST. The book teaches: the proof server generates the proof, consuming DUST from the user's balance. The circuit must be optimized to minimize costs while maintaining privacy. This completes the full system.
visualHint: DUST balance being deducted for proof generation

title: System architecture overview
text: The book presents the full architecture: (1) Ledger stores Merkle root of eligible voters, commitment to vote, and nullifier set. (2) User device creates witness data. (3) Proof server generates ZK proof. (4) Circuit verifies everything.

title: The complete circuit
text: The circuit does: (1) Verify Merkle proof for eligibility. (2) Verify vote commitment is valid. (3) Verify nullifier is unique. (4) Assert all conditions are met. The book shows this combines all concepts in one verification.
visualHint: Circuit diagram with all verification steps

title: Privacy preserved at each step
text: The book emphasizes: voter identity hidden (Merkle proof), vote content hidden (commitment), vote count verifiable (disclose), no double-voting (nullifier). Each step preserves a different aspect of privacy while enabling verification.
visualHint: Privacy shields at each step of the flow

title: The challenge parameters
text: The boss battle has specific requirements: handle 1000 eligible voters, support 3 candidates, prevent double-voting, keep votes private, and provide a public tally. You must optimize the circuit to minimize DUST while meeting all requirements.
visualHint: Challenge parameters panel with all requirements

title: The boss battle begins
text: It's time. The book sets up the final challenge: implement the complete voting system. You'll need to create the circuit that verifies eligibility, encrypts the vote, prevents double-voting, and provides a tally. This is everything you've learned.
visualHint: Start button or opening battle scene

title: Your toolkit for victory
text: You have all the tools: witness for private inputs, assert for logic, disclose for selective reveal, nullifier for uniqueness, DUST for cost, Merkle for membership. The book reminds you: each has its place. Choose wisely.
visualHint: Toolkit with all course concepts as tools

title: Optimization strategy
text: The boss has a twist: minimize DUST while maintaining privacy. The book teaches: optimize circuits by reducing constraints, use efficient hash functions, batch proofs where possible. Victory goes to those who balance privacy with efficiency.

title: Congratulations, Guardian
text: The book concludes: you've mastered self-sovereign identity, ledger vs witness, verifiable identity, zero-knowledge proofs, nullifiers, DUST costs, commitments, and Merkle trees. You are now a Crypto Guardian, ready to build privacy-preserving systems. Welcome to the Midnight.
visualHint: Celebration with guardian shield or trophy
